partner_context.their_ambition: You are Indonesia's home-grown super-app — Gojek, the mobility and payments core of GoTo, the largest digital ecosystem in the world's fourth-most-populous nation. Mobility is your founding business, and after sharpening focus (exiting Vietnam in 2024 and Thailand in 2021) your 2026 playbook is to deepen and defend your two markets — your vast Indonesian home and your strategic Singapore showcase — and drive them to durable profitability.
partner_context.their_pressure: Ride-hail on land in your home market is maturing and fiercely contested with Grab. Your next leg of high-margin growth comes from new surfaces, not from squeezing the road — and you operate across the largest archipelago on earth, where 17,000+ islands and the busiest international ferry corridors run on slow, ageing, accident-prone diesel boats that no super-app has ever monetized.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Water is the transport surface of Indonesia itself — and no super-app owns it. Navier turns it into a tier in your app: a software-defined foiling fleet, booked in Gojek, premium-priced, on the densest island crossings and cross-border corridors in the archipelago you call home — the same network model already ramping at scale in the Maldives.

hero.title: Gojek × Navier — the super-app, on the water of the world's largest archipelago
hero.subtitle: Indonesia is 17,000+ islands and Gojek is its home-grown super-app. Water is the transport surface no one owns yet.
hero.what_we_do_together: We launch a Gojek-branded foiling water tier across Indonesia's densest island crossings and cross-border corridors — booked in-app, premium-priced, category-defining in the largest archipelago on earth. Navier brings the software-defined hydrofoiling fleet and the network playbook now proven in the Maldives; Gojek brings the demand, the app, GoPay, and home-turf reach across Indonesia and Singapore. Together we turn slow, weather-exposed, accident-prone ferry crossings into fast, smooth, safe in-app water trips — and claim the category in the one country where water is the nation.

why_now: Foiling lifts the hull clear of the water: faster, dramatically more efficient per passenger-mile, smooth and near-silent, hybrid-capable with no charging-infrastructure dependency, and autonomy-ready. A ~100-vessel network is already ramping in the Maldives (WSJ/Bloomberg, 2026), Singapore's regulator is mandating clean harbour craft from 2030, and Indonesia's most-trafficked crossings (Bali↔Nusa, Batam↔Singapore) are infamous for slow, accident-prone diesel boats. The category gets claimed cluster-by-cluster — and the world's largest archipelago is the surface that matters most.
multimodal_fit: Gojek already runs the hardest parts: real-time demand, dispatch, dynamic pricing, GoPay, and a GoRide/GoCar driver-partner network across Indonesia and Singapore. A foiling water tier slots straight in — same app, same wallet, captain-partners instead of driver-partners, the water leg booked door-to-door with the GoRide to and from the pier. Navier is simply the missing surface in a multimodal map Gojek already operates across the archipelago.

proof_points.claim: Mobility and on-demand is GoTo's largest revenue engine.
proof_points.evidence: On-demand services (Gojek's mobility + delivery) generated IDR 12.36 trillion in FY2025 — ~67.5% of GoTo's IDR 18.3T revenue (+24% YoY). A premium in-app water tier compounds the segment that already carries the company.

proof_points.claim: The super-app the water tier plugs into is now at scale and turning profitable.
proof_points.evidence: GoTo posted IDR 124 trillion of group GTV in 2025 with core GTV up 49% YoY and adjusted EBITDA of ~IDR 2T (ahead of guidance), then delivered its first-ever quarterly net profit in Q1 2026.

proof_points.claim: Indonesia's regulators are pulling marine toward clean fleets.
proof_points.evidence: Indonesia's Ministry of Transportation prioritises maritime decarbonisation toward a net-zero-by-2060 goal, with a national electric-boat program piloted in Jakarta's Thousand Islands; on the cross-border side, Singapore mandates fully electric / net-zero-fuel new harbour craft from 2030.
proof_points.source: ICCT / Kemenhub 2025; Maritime & Port Authority of Singapore

proof_points.claim: The cross-border demand already exists — on diesel boats.
proof_points.evidence: Batam's ferry terminals alone served ~4.2 million passengers in the first half of 2024 (+6% YoY), the bulk of it crossing to and from Singapore on one of the world's busiest international ferry corridors — both Gojek markets.

objections.concern: Is the range enough across an archipelago?
objections.response: The dense everyday crossings — Jakarta's Thousand Islands (~12 nm), Bali↔Nusa (~12 nm), Singapore↔Batam/Bintan (~12-22 nm), Labuan Bajo↔Komodo (~18 nm) — all sit well inside the Pioneer II 70 nm all-electric envelope. The long eastern frontier legs (Sangihe-Talaud, Raja Ampat outliers, Flores) run on the Quanta-LR hybrid at 700 nm range, with no charging infrastructure required anywhere.

objections.concern: Indonesian crossings have a serious safety reputation problem.
objections.response: That is exactly the opening. The 2025 Bali Strait ferry sinking is the kind of event that makes the status quo untenable. Foils lift the hull clear of the surface so the ride is smooth where displacement boats pound; software-defined controls, a clear first-of-class certification path, and an operating record across the US and the Maldives make a Navier tier the safe, premium alternative travellers will actively choose.

objections.concern: Can this be profitable, not just a flagship?
objections.response: On-demand is already GoTo's biggest revenue engine; a foiling tier monetises premium crossings users take today on unmonetised diesel ferries, at a price point the affluent leisure and cross-border flows support. It rides the same app, wallet, dispatch and pricing rails Gojek already runs — captain-partners instead of driver-partners — so the marginal cost of adding the surface is low.

objections.concern: Monsoon and open-water seasonality?
objections.response: Sheltered-strait routing plus the Quanta-LR's range give the network the flexibility to keep running and reposition through monsoon windows, and the foiling ride is more weather-tolerant than the ferries it replaces — that reliability is the premium.

phases.label: Phase 1 — Bali beachhead
phases.rationale: Start where the water demand is densest, most affluent, and already in-app. Bali's Nusa-Gili transfers are the most painful, highest-margin water trips Gojek's users take today — the perfect first cluster to prove the silent, no-seasickness foiling arrival.
phases.narrative: Bali is the proof market: a dense, affluent, app-native flow of transfers across the Badung Strait where today's options are slow, wet bangka boats and pounding fast-craft. Five N30s on the Nusa-Gili corridors show Gojek users a water layer that feels like the rest of the app — booked, priced, and tracked in-app.

phases.label: Phase 2 — Jakarta commute + the Singapore crossing
phases.rationale: Layer in the daily-commute proof (Jakarta's Thousand Islands + chronic gridlock that water bypasses) and the marquee cross-border crossing Batam/Bintan↔Singapore — Gojek's home flow meeting Southeast Asia's busiest international ferry corridor.
phases.narrative: Jakarta turns the story from leisure to daily mobility: the Thousand Islands and a waterfront that a foil can cross while the toll road sits still. Simultaneously the Riau↔Singapore crossing — millions of trips a year — gets a quiet, fast, premium tier inside an app travellers on both sides already hold.

phases.label: Phase 3 — The eastern archipelago
phases.rationale: Carry the network east into the marquee marine-tourism frontiers — Komodo/Flores, North Sulawesi, Raja Ampat — where long, exposed open-water legs are exactly what the Quanta-LR hybrid was built for and where premium dive/expedition demand will pay for it.
phases.narrative: The east is where range matters: 100-plus-nautical-mile legs to Komodo, Bunaken and Raja Ampat that no all-electric craft can hold. The Quanta-LR hybrid opens these silently and at speed, turning multi-hour boat slogs into the best part of the trip — and putting Gojek's brand on the water in Indonesia's most photographed seascapes.

phases.label: Phase 4 — The whole archipelago coastal map
phases.rationale: With clusters proven across west, central and east, the water layer becomes a standing in-app product across the world's largest archipelago — 17,000 islands where the road simply ends at the shore.
phases.narrative: By Phase 4 the water is just another Gojek surface: open the app anywhere on Indonesia's 80,000 km of coastline and a silent foiling boat is a tap away. The country whose geography is its biggest mobility constraint becomes the one with the most advanced water-mobility network on earth.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet (Pioneer II + Quanta-LR hybrid), the network and operations playbook proven at scale in the Maldives, captain-partner training, and the first-of-class certification path for Indonesian and Singaporean waters.
the_ask.partner_brings: You bring demand and dispatch through the Gojek app, GoPay, the brand, the captain-partner model, and the home-turf regulatory relationships across Indonesia and Singapore.
the_ask.next_step: A Bali or Jakarta pilot MOU: co-define the in-app foiling water tier on three corridors, then scale across the archipelago cluster by cluster.

close.title: One app. 17,000 islands. The water layer of Indonesia's super-app.
close.body: Bali proves it, Jakarta Bay turns it into daily mobility, the Singapore crossing makes it cross-border, and Komodo, Sulawesi and Raja Ampat carry it east across the frontier. From there the same playbook extends across every island crossing Gojek already serves — the water layer of the world's largest archipelago, booked entirely inside the super-app.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged in Gojek's own backyard: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out); a ~100-vessel network is ramping in the Maldives; and Indonesia's busiest, most safety-troubled crossings — Bali↔Nusa, Batam↔Singapore — are ready to be switched onto a clean foiling tier in the app Indonesians already live in.

network_thesis.body: Indonesia is 17,000+ islands across 5,000 km of ocean — the most water-defined nation on earth — and Gojek is its home-grown super-app, operating across the archipelago and in Singapore. The same in-app foiling tier proven in the Maldives extends to every island crossing and cross-border corridor Gojek serves: pick one market to prove it, or roll the recommended sequence below. The fleet, the app integration, and the captain-partner model are identical everywhere.
network_thesis.how_to_read: Each card is a real, ready market. Start with Jakarta — Gojek's founding city and cleanest first proof point — or pick any cluster. The phased sequence below is our recommended path, not the only one.

The same fleet and in-app tier extend to every island crossing and cross-border corridor Gojek already serves.

The bay and islands are served today by slow, weather-exposed wooden ferries from Marina Ancol and Muara Angke. This is the water layer of Gojek's home city: an in-app foiling tier that turns Jakarta Bay into a commuter and leisure highway and the Thousand Islands into seamless premium hops — the cleanest possible proof point in the market Gojek owns most completely.

markets.label: Komodo & Flores
markets.summary: Labuan Bajo, the gateway to Komodo National Park, is Indonesia's fastest-rising marquee destination — a government 'super-priority' tourism zone with a new international airport and a booming liveaboard and day-boat market. Today the Komodo park, the pink-sand beaches, Padar and the surrounding Flores arc are served almost entirely by slow diesel cruise boats and phinisi schooners. This is a premium island-hopping market tailor-made for a clean foiling tier: an in-app Gojek water layer that turns the multi-hour diesel transfers around Komodo into fast, smooth, low-impact hops through one of the planet's most spectacular seascapes.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.

markets.label: Eastern Indonesia Frontier
markets.summary: Eastern Indonesia — North Sulawesi (Manado/Bunaken/Likupang), Wakatobi, Raja Ampat in West Papua — is the country's diving and marine-tourism frontier: world-class seascapes spread across vast open water, served today only by liveaboards, infrequent flights and slow boats. As Gojek deepens its national super-app reach, this is the long-range frontier where Quanta-LR's 700 nm hybrid range turns scattered, hard-to-reach islands into a connected in-app network — a clean foiling layer across the planet's richest marine biodiversity.

hero.title: Eastern Indonesia's marine frontier, connected.
hero.subtitle: Quanta-LR turns scattered world-class seascapes into a connected in-app foiling network.
hero.what_we_do_together: Gojek brings expanding national super-app reach; Navier brings the Quanta-LR hybrid that crosses the open water between Indonesia's eastern islands. Together we connect the diving frontier — Bunaken, Wakatobi, Raja Ampat — as a clean in-app network.

partner_context.their_ambition: Gojek is deepening its super-app footprint across Indonesia's eastern provinces as connectivity and tourism investment spread beyond Java and Bali.
partner_context.their_pressure: Eastern Indonesia's marquee marine destinations are spectacular but fragmented — reachable only by liveaboards, infrequent flights and slow diesel boats, with vast open-water gaps and no clean, scheduled, premium water mobility.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: A foiling water tier built around Quanta-LR's 700 nm hybrid range: clean long-range runs that connect the eastern islands into an in-app network, with Pioneer II hops within each marine-park cluster — opening the diving frontier without new infrastructure.

markets.why_now: Eastern Indonesia's marine tourism is booming on the back of Likupang's super-priority status and Raja Ampat's global fame, the islands are separated by open water no scheduled clean craft serves, and Gojek is expanding nationally. Quanta-LR's range makes the frontier addressable.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Eastern Indonesia's marine tourism is booming on the back of Likupang's super-priority status and Raja Ampat's global fame, the islands are separated by vast open water no scheduled clean craft serves, and Gojek is expanding its national super-app reach.

proof_points.claim: Likupang is a national super-priority destination.
proof_points.evidence: North Sulawesi's Likupang was named one of Indonesia's five super-priority tourism destinations, anchoring marine tourism around Manado and Bunaken.
proof_points.source: Indonesia Ministry of Tourism & Creative Economy

proof_points.claim: Raja Ampat is a global marine icon.
proof_points.evidence: Raja Ampat holds the richest recorded marine biodiversity on earth, drawing high-value divers worldwide despite difficult access.

proof_points.claim: The frontier runs on liveaboards and slow boats.
proof_points.evidence: Eastern Indonesia's marine destinations are served almost entirely by liveaboards, infrequent flights and diesel boats — no clean scheduled water tier exists.

proof_points.claim: Quanta-LR's range fits the geography.
proof_points.evidence: The open-water gaps between eastern islands routinely exceed Pioneer II's range — Quanta-LR's 700 nm hybrid range is what makes a connected network possible without new infrastructure.

objections.concern: The distances and open water are extreme.
objections.response: This is precisely the Quanta-LR use case — 700 nm hybrid range with no charging dependence — while Pioneer II covers the sheltered marine-park hops within each cluster.

objections.concern: Shore infrastructure in the east is minimal.
objections.response: That is the point: Quanta-LR needs no charging infrastructure and Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal, so the frontier is addressable without building anything new.

objections.concern: Demand is seasonal and dive-led.
objections.response: A flexible software-defined fleet scales with the dive season and repositions between clusters; the in-app Gojek layer aggregates demand that is today scattered across many small operators.

phases.label: Phase 1 — North Sulawesi marine parks (Pioneer II)
phases.narrative: Launch around Manado — clean low-wake Pioneer II hops to Bunaken, Siladen and across to the Lembeh Strait — putting North Sulawesi's super-priority marine parks on an in-app foiling tier built around the Likupang gateway.
phases.rationale: A super-priority destination with world-class diving and no clean premium water tier.

phases.label: Phase 2 — Raja Ampat cluster (Pioneer II + Quanta-LR)
phases.narrative: Open the Raja Ampat cluster — Sorong to Waisai by Pioneer II, then Quanta-LR long-range links out to Wayag's karst cones and the Misool reserves — connecting the dispersed island groups of Earth's richest reef into an in-app network.
phases.rationale: A global marine icon with difficult, fragmented access — the showcase Quanta-LR cluster.

phases.label: Phase 3 — Eastern long-range network (Quanta-LR)
phases.narrative: Knit the eastern frontier together with Quanta-LR line-hauls — Manado to the Sangihe-Talaud chain, Wakatobi to the Makassar super-hub — so the scattered marine destinations become a connected long-range foiling network in the Gojek app.
phases.rationale: Connecting the eastern clusters via Quanta-LR line-hauls turns isolated destinations into a national-scale network.

close.title: The frontier, connected.
close.body: North Sulawesi first, then Raja Ampat and the eastern long-range network — the planet's richest seascapes, linked by clean foiling water in-app.

end_state.headline: A connected clean foiling network across Indonesia's eastern marine frontier.
